title_en: Hong Kong Xinnuo Investment Co., Ltd. — Application for Enforcement Reconsideration
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where a third party raises an objection claiming ownership of the subject matter of execution, the objection shall be reviewed in accordance with the procedure provided in Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law. If the third party or any party is dissatisfied with the enforcement ruling, relief shall be sought through litigation proceedings. The third party shall not be treated as an interested party and subject to review under the procedure provided in Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, nor shall the party be granted the right to apply for reconsideration. Otherwise, it constitutes an error in the application of law and a violation of statutory procedures, which shall be corrected.

full_text_en:
Hong Kong Xinnuo Investment Co., Ltd. Application for Reconsideration of Enforcement Ruling

[Ruling Summary]

I. Where a third party raises an objection claiming ownership of the subject matter of enforcement, the objection shall be reviewed in accordance with the procedure provided for in Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law. If the third party or any party disagrees with the enforcement ruling, relief shall be sought through litigation proceedings. The third party shall not be treated as an interested party and the objection shall not be reviewed under the procedure provided for in Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, with the right to apply for reconsideration granted to the parties; otherwise, it constitutes an error in the application of the law and a violation of legal procedures, which shall be corrected.

II. If a procedural objection raised by a third party is unrelated to its objection claiming ownership of the subject matter of enforcement, it may, where conditions are met, be reviewed under the procedure provided for in Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law as an interested party, and handled separately from the substantive dispute; if the procedural objection raised by the third party is closely related to the substantive objection, directly or indirectly addressing the ownership issue of the same subject matter of enforcement, and where the third party simultaneously raises a substantive objection, the two objections shall be reviewed together under the procedure provided for in Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, so as to reduce the litigation burden on the parties.

III. An objection raised separately by the judgment debtor shall be reviewed under the procedure provided for in Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law. However, if the objection raised by the judgment debtor essentially supports the third party's claim of substantive rights over the subject matter of enforcement, the judgment debtor's objection shall not be reviewed separately but shall be resolved together in the course of reviewing the third party's objection.

Enforcement Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Zhi Fu Zi No. 13

Applicant for Reconsideration (Enforcement Applicant): Hong Kong Xinnuo Investment Co., Ltd. Address: Room 1103-5, United Deer Island Building, 138 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong.

Legal Representative: Zu Li, Executive Director of the Company.

Judgment Debtor: Shandong Animal By-Products Import and Export Corporation. Address: No. 51 Taiping Road, Qingdao City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Zhaoxing, General Manager of the Company.

Third Party: Shandong Department of Commerce (formerly Shandong Department of Foreign Economic and Trade Cooperation). Address: No. 6 Liyang Street, Shizhong District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

The applicant for reconsideration, Hong Kong Xinnuo Investment Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3 of the Shandong High People's Court, applied to this Court for reconsideration. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct a review, which is now concluded.

The enforcement court, Shandong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Shandong High Court), found the following facts: In the case of the dispute over a loan contract between Qingdao Office of China Orient Asset Management Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Orient Qingdao Office) and Shandong Animal By-Products Import and Export Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Animal By-Products Company), which was accepted by Qingdao Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Qingdao Intermediate Court), during the trial, on May 21, 2001, Qingdao Intermediate Court issued a property preservation ruling (2001) Qing Zhi Zi No. 52-1, sealing up the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building, located at No. 51 Taiping Road, Qingdao City, owned by Animal By-Products Company. On May 25, 2001, after Animal By-Products Company raised objections to jurisdiction and sealing, the case was transferred to Shandong High Court for trial. On September 12, 2001, Shandong Department of Foreign Economic and Trade Cooperation filed an objection to property preservation with Shandong High Court. On October 17, 2001, Shandong High Court issued a civil ruling (2001) Lu Jing Chu Zi No. 16-1, stating that due to land, fire safety, and other reasons, no title certificate had been issued for Shandong International Trade Building, and all units using the building only had the right of use. During the construction of the building, Animal By-Products Company actually contributed RMB 8,261,300 to the construction of the building. The company currently uses rooms 1709, 1711, 1712, and 1713 on the 17th floor of the building for office purposes, with a total area of 422 square meters. Finding that the objection raised by Shandong Department of Foreign Economic and Trade Cooperation was partially justified, the court ruled: 1. The sealing of the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building by Qingdao Intermediate Court is lifted; 2. The four offices on the 17th floor of Shandong International Trade Building used by Animal By-Products Company (rooms 1709, 1711, 1712, and 1713, with a total area of 422 square meters) are sealed up.

On November 9, 2001, Shandong High Court issued a civil judgment (2001) Lu Jing Chu Zi No. 16, ordering Animal By-Products Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 50 million to Orient Qingdao Office. After the judgment took effect, as Animal By-Products Company failed to perform its obligations in accordance with the law, Orient Qingdao Office applied to Shandong High Court for compulsory enforcement on January 10, 2002. During the enforcement process, on July 21, 2006, Hong Kong Xinnuo Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinnuo Company) acquired the claims in this case from Orient Qingdao Office and applied to Shandong High Court for a change of the enforcement applicant to itself, and also requested Shandong High Court to seal up the four offices on the 17th floor of Shandong International Trade Building owned by Animal By-Products Company. After review, Shandong High Court changed Xinnuo Company to be the enforcement applicant in this case in accordance with the law, and at the same time took sealing measures against the properties on the 17th floor of Shandong International Trade Building. On September 20, 2006, Xinnuo Company further applied to Shandong High Court, requesting to seal up all the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building owned by Animal By-Products Company. On September 25 of the same year, Shandong High Court issued a civil ruling (2002) Lu Zhi Zi No. 3-4, preliminarily sealing up the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building (the properties had no title certificate).

On September 20, 2011, Shandong High Court issued an enforcement ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3-3, continuing the preliminary sealing of all properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building, located at No. 51 Taiping Road, Qingdao City, owned by Animal By-Products Company. The sealing period was one year, from September 25, 2011, to September 24, 2012. On September 18, 2012, Shandong High Court issued an enforcement ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3-4, continuing the preliminary sealing of all properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building, located at No. 51 Taiping Road, Qingdao City, owned by Animal By-Products Company. The sealing period was one year, from September 25, 2012, to September 24, 2013. Animal By-Products Company and Shandong Department of Commerce, dissatisfied, separately filed written objections with Shandong High Court, claiming that it was improper for Shandong High Court to conduct a preliminary sealing without evidence after having lifted the sealing of the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building; that the ownership of the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building belongs to Shandong Department of Foreign Economic and Trade Cooperation (the predecessor of Shandong Department of Commerce), and the sealing of these properties should be lifted.

Shandong High Court further found that Shandong International Trade Building was an office building jointly constructed by eight companies directly under the then Shandong Foreign Trade Bureau stationed in Qingdao, approved by the Shandong Provincial People's Government and the Shandong Provincial Planning Commission in June 1990. The former Shandong Foreign Trade Bureau specifically established a building preparatory organization, namely Shandong International Trade Building Management Company, to unify the raising of funds and the management of the building construction. According to the allocation plan at that time, Animal By-Products Company was allocated the 17th to 21st floors of the building. It was found that Animal By-Products Company contributed a total of RMB 8,261,300.

On October 26, 1992, the Shandong Foreign Trade Bureau held a meeting of the Joint Construction Leadership Group for Shandong Foreign Trade Office Buildings, which determined the allocation plan and the establishment of a Building Management Committee, under which a Building Management Company was set up to be specifically responsible for the management of the building. Item 4 of the meeting indicated that the building project required an expenditure of RMB 171 million by the end of 1992, and units that were in arrears with their investment payments were required to pay them in full by the end of 1992; otherwise, they would be deemed to have automatically given up, and the originally allocated floors would be sold by the building preparatory office to raise funds for construction. At the same time, the meeting emphasized that due to the prolonged construction period and rising raw material prices, additional investment would be needed for the building construction. For units that truly lacked the ability to raise funds, had poor performance, and were unable to obtain bank loans, the Foreign Trade Bureau commissioned Shandong Foreign Trade General Corporation to provide a unified loan of RMB 60 million, and requested that the borrowing units sign a loan agreement with Shandong Foreign Trade General Corporation by November 10, 1992; otherwise, the originally allocated floors would be otherwise disposed of.

After the meeting, Animal By-Products Company neither paid its investment in full nor signed a loan agreement with Shandong Foreign Trade General Corporation. On July 25, 1994, Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission held a director's office meeting, in which Item 2 indicated that the construction of Shandong International Trade Building was basically completed, the matters determined by the former preparatory leadership group remained valid, and no individuals could arbitrarily change them. The meeting emphasized that there were still units (including Animal By-Products Company) in arrears, and a deadline was set for them to pay the arrears in full by August 10, 1994. After the meeting, Animal By-Products Company still failed to pay its arrears. In May 1998, the director's office meeting of Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission decided to give a final notice for the collection of construction funds, requiring payment by the end of May 1998, failing which the ownership would belong to the units that had advanced the payments. On June 8, 1998, Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission issued an official document notifying: "Due to the long span of the building construction period and the unclear investment rights and obligations or insufficient investment by some provincial specialized foreign trade and economic companies, the ownership of the building belongs to Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission."

Shandong High Court opined in its review: First, although the properties involved did not have title certificates, from the process of their formation, Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission had the ultimate decision-making power regarding the allocation of the properties. According to the approval documents of the Shandong Provincial People's Government and the Shandong Provincial Planning Commission, Shandong International Trade Building was formed by eight units, including Animal By-Products Company, under Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission. The allocation plan at that time was that Animal By-Products Company would receive the 17th to 21st floors, but after contributing RMB 8.26 million, the company had no subsequent funds to invest, and after multiple demands for payment, it still did not pay off the arrears. In June 1998, Shandong Provincial Foreign Economic and Trade Commission issued a document changing the 17th to 21st floors that Animal By-Products Company should have received to four rooms on the 17th floor, from which it could be determined that Animal By-Products Company only received the aforementioned four rooms. Moreover, Animal By-Products Company did not raise any objection thereafter, which should be deemed as its acceptance of this allocation plan. Second, the original enforcement applicant, Orient Qingdao Office, did not raise any objection after receiving the civil ruling (2001) Lu Jing Chu Zi No. 16-1 of Shandong High Court. In 2005, before selling the claims in this case, its asset assessment also clarified that Animal By-Products Company only had four rooms in Shandong International Trade Building, which should be deemed as Orient Qingdao Office's recognition of the scope of all assets of the judgment debtor Animal By-Products Company. Xinnuo Company is the transferee of the claims in this case. After acquiring the claims, on the one hand, it enjoys rights to the amount of the claims transferred; on the other hand, when exercising the claims, it should also be bound by the scope of the original enforcement applicant's rights, i.e., where the original enforcement applicant has recognized the scope of the assets of the judgment debtor Animal By-Products Company, Xinnuo Company, after acquiring the claims, can only exercise its rights within the scope of assets recognized by the original rights holder. Its claim for rights to the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building exceeds its scope of rights and should not be supported.

Shandong High Court held that the grounds for the objectors' objections were established and should be supported. It then issued an enforcement ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3 on November 29, 2012, in accordance with Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2007) and Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in Enforcement Procedures, ruling to revoke the Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3-3 of Shandong High Court and lift the sealing of the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building (excluding the four rooms 1709, 1711, 1712, and 1713). On December 6, 2012, Xinnuo Company raised an objection with Shandong High Court, arguing that there were major issues with the Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3, that the true intent of Shandong High Court was incomprehensible, and requesting clarification. On December 14, 2012, Shandong High Court issued another ruling to correct the text of the Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3 of Shandong High Court to: "Revoke the Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3-4 of this Court, and lift the sealing of the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building (excluding the four rooms 1709, 1711, 1712, and 1713)."

Dissatisfied with the above ruling, Xinnuo Company applied to this Court for reconsideration, requesting the revocation of the Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3 of Shandong High Court, the lawful preliminary sealing and auction of the properties on the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building, located at No. 51 Taiping Road, Qingdao City, owned by Animal By-Products Company, and that Shandong Department of Commerce compensate Xinnuo Company for the losses caused by its objection, within the value of the properties involved. The main reasons were: First, there were two obvious document errors in the ruling: the document number of the enforcement ruling revoked was unrelated to this case or did not exist at all. The objector in this case was Shandong Department of Commerce, not Animal By-Products Company. Second, the ruling erred in the application of law, as it should not have applied Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2007) but should have applied Article 204. Third, the original court erred in fact-finding, lacking evidentiary support. Shandong Department of Commerce did not provide any evidence proving that the 17th to 21st floors originally allocated to Animal By-Products Company were changed to four rooms on the 17th floor. Orient Qingdao Office had previously requested the original court to investigate and collect evidence to lawfully determine the ownership of the properties involved. Fourth, the original court's conclusion was erroneous. The properties involved should belong to Animal By-Products Company, and Shandong Department of Commerce was not the owner of the properties involved. Document (1990) Lu Zheng Han Zi No. 14 of the Shandong Provincial People's Government had already determined the ownership of the eight joint construction units, and the later document of Shandong Department of Commerce could not override this document. Shandong Department of Commerce and Animal By-Products Company were on equal footing in the joint construction of the building, and Shandong Department of Commerce did not have the authority to place Animal By-Products Company's properties under its own name; the ownership of the properties involved could not be determined based on Document (1998) No. 181 issued by Shandong Department of Commerce. There was no evidence that Animal By-Products Company's collective construction funds were not paid in full. Even if Animal By-Products Company owed construction funds, it could not transfer ownership to the units that advanced the funds. The properties involved were provided by Animal By-Products Company for use by others free of charge. According to the principle of "who invests, benefits," the value of the properties owned by Animal By-Products Company far exceeded the value of just four rooms. It was erroneous to rely on the content of the assessment report of Orient Qingdao Office before the transfer of the claims to determine that Animal By-Products Company only had ownership of four rooms. Fifth, the original court's revocation of the sealing of the properties involved seriously harmed the lawful rights and interests of the applicant.

This Court is of the opinion that the focus of the reconsideration review in this case is the issue of the review procedure regarding the written objections separately filed by Animal By-Products Company and Shandong Department of Commerce with Shandong High Court on the same grounds, in dissatisfaction with the enforcement ruling of Shandong High Court.

Regarding the review procedure for Shandong Department of Commerce's objection: The main reason for the objection filed by the third party Shandong Department of Commerce, claiming that the court should lift the sealing, was the second item of its objection, i.e., that the ownership of the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building belonged to it, and therefore the court could not seal them up as assets of Animal By-Products Company. This objection is a claim for ownership of the subject matter of enforcement. According to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, "During the enforcement process, if a third party submits a written objection to the subject matter of enforcement, the People's Court shall review it within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the written objection. If the reasons are established, the court shall rule to suspend enforcement of that subject matter; if the reasons are not established, the court shall rule to reject the objection. If the third party or a party is dissatisfied with the ruling and believes that the original judgment or ruling is erroneous, it shall proceed in accordance with the trial supervision procedure; if unrelated to the original judgment or ruling, it may file a lawsuit with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of service of the ruling." The enforcement court, Shandong High Court, treated Shandong Department of Commerce as an interested party and applied Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2007) and Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in Enforcement Procedures to review the objection and granted the parties the right to apply for reconsideration, which is clearly an error in the application of the law, a violation of legal procedures, and should be corrected. As for the first objection raised by Shandong Department of Commerce, i.e., that it was improper for Shandong High Court to conduct a preliminary sealing without evidence after having lawfully lifted the sealing of the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building, although it is an objection concerning enforcement procedures, in essence, it is based on Shandong Department of Commerce's substantive claim of ownership over the 17th to 21st floors of Shandong International Trade Building. In this case, the two objections raised by Shandong Department of Commerce both directly or indirectly address the ownership issue of the same subject matter of enforcement and are closely related. Applying different review procedures to them would only increase the litigation burden on the parties. Therefore, the first objection raised by Shandong Department of Commerce should also be reviewed under the procedure provided for in Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Regarding the review procedure for the objection raised by Animal By-Products Company: Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a party or an interested party believes that an enforcement act violates legal provisions, it may submit a written objection to the People's Court responsible for enforcement. If a party or an interested party submits a written objection, the People's Court shall review it within fifteen days from the date of receipt. If the reasons are established, the court shall rule to revoke or correct the act; if the reasons are not established, the court shall rule to reject the objection. If a party or an interested party is dissatisfied with the ruling, it may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration within ten days from the date of service of the ruling." The objection raised by the judgment debtor Animal By-Products Company, on the ground that the enforcement act violated legal provisions, could have been reviewed under the procedure provided for in Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. However, in this case, the objection raised by Animal By-Products Company essentially supports the third party Shandong Department of Commerce's claim of ownership over the subject matter of enforcement. If the objections with the same content raised by Animal By-Products Company and Shandong Department of Commerce were to be reviewed under different procedures, resulting in different avenues of relief, the procedural interests of the parties would be harmed. Moreover, given that the third party Shandong Department of Commerce has already raised an objection claiming substantive rights, the objection raised by the judgment debtor Animal By-Products Company lacks practical benefit. Therefore, the objection raised by Animal By-Products Company should not be reviewed separately but should be resolved together in the course of reviewing Shandong Department of Commerce's objection.

In summary, the original ruling erred in the application of law and violated legal procedures. This Court, by reference to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rules as follows:

I. The Enforcement Ruling (2002) Lu Zhi (Hui) Zi No. 3 of Shandong High People's Court is hereby revoked.

II. The case is remanded to Shandong High People's Court for a new review and handling.

This ruling shall take effect immediately upon service.

Presiding Judge: Zhao Jinshan

Acting Judge: Pan Yongfeng

Acting Judge: Ge Hongtao

November 5, 2013

Clerk: Chen Haixia

[Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Zhao Jinshan: born in 1970, Doctor of Laws. Has served as an Adjudicator of the Supreme People's Court since 2010.
